mcq.q: If n(A) = 35, n(B) = 17 and n(A ∪ B) = 38, then n(A ∩ B) =
mcq.explain: From n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B): n(A ∩ B) = 35 + 17 − 38 = 14. Whenever n(A) + n(B) is more than n(A ∪ B), the excess is exactly the common part counted twice.
mcq.fast: Overlap = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∪ B).

mcq.q: If n(A) = 40, n(B) = 38 and n(A ∩ B) = 34, then n(A ∪ B) =
mcq.explain: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B) = 40 + 38 − 34 = 44. The elements in both sets are counted twice when we add n(A) and n(B), so they are subtracted once. Adding only (78) double-counts the common part.
mcq.fast: Add the two sets, subtract the overlap once.

mcq.q: In a group of 302 people, 128 like Hindi newspapers, 147 like English newspapers and 32 like both. How many like neither?
mcq.explain: People who like at least one = 128 + 147 − 32 = 243. Neither = total − at least one = 302 − 243 = 59. Subtracting 128 and 147 from 302 without adding back the 32 who like both removes them twice.

mcq.q: In a group of 263 people, 145 like cricket, 56 like football and 27 like both. How many like neither?
mcq.explain: People who like at least one = 145 + 56 − 27 = 174. Neither = total − at least one = 263 − 174 = 89. Subtracting 145 and 56 from 263 without adding back the 27 who like both removes them twice.
n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) − n(A ∩ B) − n(B ∩ C) − n(C ∩ A) + n(A ∩ B ∩ C) = 171 − 75 + 5 = 101. The triple overlap is added three times, subtracted three times, so it must be added back once.
mcq.fast: Add singles, subtract pairs, add the triple.

mcq.explain: n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) − n(A ∩ B) − n(B ∩ C) − n(C ∩ A) + n(A ∩ B ∩ C) = 208 − 121 + 23 = 110. The triple overlap is added three times, subtracted three times, so it must be added back once.
mcq.fast: Add singles, subtract pairs, add the triple.

mcq.q: A is the set of letters of the word "MANAGEMENT". The number of proper subsets of A is:
mcq.explain: A set lists each element once, so A has the 6 distinct letters {A, E, G, M, N, T}, not 10. A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets and 2ⁿ − 1 proper subsets (all except A itself). So 2^6 − 1 = 63.
mcq.fast: Count distinct letters first, then 2ⁿ (minus 1 for proper subsets).

mcq.q: A is the set of letters of the word "COMMERCE". The number of proper subsets of A is:
mcq.explain: A set lists each element once, so A has the 5 distinct letters {C, E, M, O, R}, not 8. A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets and 2ⁿ − 1 proper subsets (all except A itself). So 2^5 − 1 = 31.
mcq.fast: Count distinct letters first, then 2ⁿ (minus 1 for proper subsets).

mcq.q: If A has 6 elements and B has 4 elements, the number of relations from A to B is:
mcq.explain: A relation from A to B is any subset of A × B. A × B has 6 × 4 = 24 ordered pairs, so the number of subsets (relations) is 2^24 = 1,67,77,216. This count includes the empty relation and A × B itself.
mcq.topic: Relations: domain, range, inverse and types
mcq.fast: Relations = 2^(mn): every ordered pair is either in or out.

mcq.q: If A has 6 elements and B has 2 elements, the number of elements in A × B is:
mcq.explain: A × B is the set of all ordered pairs (a, b) with a from A and b from B. Each of the 6 elements of A pairs with each of the 2 elements of B, so n(A × B) = 6 × 2 = 12. Order inside a pair matters, but the count is still the product.
mcq.topic: Ordered pairs and the Cartesian product
mcq.fast: n(A × B) = n(A) × n(B).

mcq.q: How many members does {x : x is a multiple of 6 and 56 < x < 89} have?
mcq.explain: Write the set in roster form: {60, 66, 72, 78, 84}. The strict signs exclude 56 and 89 themselves. Counting gives 5 elements. Listing the members is the safest way to avoid including or dropping an end value.
mcq.topic: Sets, elements and the two ways of writing a set
mcq.fast: List the members quickly in roster form and count; watch whether the end values are included.

mcq.q: How many members does {x : x is a prime number and 47 < x < 63} have?
mcq.explain: Write the set in roster form: {53, 59, 61}. The strict signs exclude 47 and 63 themselves. Counting gives 3 elements. Listing the members is the safest way to avoid including or dropping an end value.
mcq.topic: Sets, elements and the two ways of writing a set
mcq.fast: List the members quickly in roster form and count; watch whether the end values are included.

mcq.q: If A = {1, 3, 11, 12} and B = {3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12}, then A Δ B (symmetric difference) is:
mcq.explain: A − B keeps elements of A that are not in B; A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A); the complement (A ∪ B)′ keeps elements of U outside both sets, which by De Morgan equals A′ ∩ B′. Applying the definition element by element gives {1, 4, 8, 9, 10}.
mcq.topic: Operations on sets and De Morgan's laws
mcq.fast: Go through the elements one by one and tick membership in A and B; keep those the operation asks for.

mcq.q: If A = {3, 4, 5, 11} and B = {1, 3, 7, 9, 10}, then A Δ B (symmetric difference) is:
mcq.explain: A − B keeps elements of A that are not in B; A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A); the complement (A ∪ B)′ keeps elements of U outside both sets, which by De Morgan equals A′ ∩ B′. Applying the definition element by element gives {1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11}.
mcq.topic: Operations on sets and De Morgan's laws
mcq.fast: Go through the elements one by one and tick membership in A and B; keep those the operation asks for.

mcq.q: On the set {1, 2, 3}, the relation R = {(1, 2), (3, 1), (3, 3)} is:
options: Symmetric but not reflexive or transitive
Reflexive but not symmetric or transitive
Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
mcq.explain: Check the three properties one at a time. Reflexive: some (x, x) is missing, so it is not reflexive. Symmetric: some (a, b) has no (b, a), so it is not symmetric. Transitive: some (a, b), (b, c) lack (a, c), so it is not transitive. Hence R is: neither reflexive, symmetric nor transitive. An equivalence relation needs all three properties.
mcq.topic: Relations: domain, range, inverse and types
mcq.fast: Check (1,1),(2,2),(3,3) first; then reverse each pair; then chain pairs end-to-start.

options: Reflexive but not symmetric or transitive
Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
mcq.explain: Check the three properties one at a time. Reflexive: some (x, x) is missing, so it is not reflexive. Symmetric: some (a, b) has no (b, a), so it is not symmetric. Transitive: some (a, b), (b, c) lack (a, c), so it is not transitive. Hence R is: neither reflexive, symmetric nor transitive. An equivalence relation needs all three properties.
mcq.topic: Relations: domain, range, inverse and types
mcq.fast: Check (1,1),(2,2),(3,3) first; then reverse each pair; then chain pairs end-to-start.

mcq.q: On the set {1, 2, 3}, the relation R = {(1, 3), (3, 3)} is:
options: Transitive but not reflexive or symmetric
Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
Symmetric but not reflexive or transitive
mcq.explain: Check the three properties one at a time. Reflexive: some (x, x) is missing, so it is not reflexive. Symmetric: some (a, b) has no (b, a), so it is not symmetric. Transitive: whenever (a, b) and (b, c) are present, (a, c) is too. Hence R is: transitive but not reflexive or symmetric. An equivalence relation needs all three properties.
mcq.topic: Relations: domain, range, inverse and types
mcq.fast: Check (1,1),(2,2),(3,3) first; then reverse each pair; then chain pairs end-to-start.

mcq.q: If f(x) = −x − 6 and g(x) = 4x², then g(f(0)) =
mcq.explain: Work from the inside out. f(0) = -6, then g(-6) = 144. Composition is generally not commutative: the other order gives -6. Multiplying f(0) and g(0) is not composition at all: in a composition the output of one function becomes the input of the other.
mcq.fast: Evaluate the inner function first, then feed the result to the outer one.

mcq.q: If f(x) = −3x + 3 and g(x) = 4x² + 1, then g(f(5)) =
mcq.explain: Work from the inside out. f(5) = -12, then g(-12) = 577. Composition is generally not commutative: the other order gives -300. Multiplying f(5) and g(5) is not composition at all: in a composition the output of one function becomes the input of the other.
mcq.fast: Evaluate the inner function first, then feed the result to the outer one.

mcq.q: If f(x) = 4x − 4, then f⁻¹(-9) =
mcq.explain: f⁻¹(-9) is the x for which f(x) = -9. Solve 4x − 4 = -9: 4x = -9 − (-4) = -5, so x = -5/4. In general f⁻¹(y) = (y − -4)/4. Computing f(-9) instead of solving f(x) = -9 is the usual mix-up.
mcq.fast: Back-substitute options into f: f(-5/4) = -9.

mcq.q: If f(x) = −3x + 1, then f⁻¹(23) =
mcq.explain: f⁻¹(23) is the x for which f(x) = 23. Solve −3x + 1 = 23: -3x = 23 − (1) = 22, so x = -22/3. In general f⁻¹(y) = (y − 1)/-3. Computing f(23) instead of solving f(x) = 23 is the usual mix-up.
mcq.fast: Back-substitute options into f: f(-22/3) = 23.

mcq.q: The value of lim (x → 2) (x⁷ − 128)/(x − 2) is:
mcq.explain: Direct substitution gives 0/0. Use the standard limit lim (x → a) (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = n·aⁿ⁻¹. With n = 7 and a = 2: 7 × (2)^6 = 448. Answering 0 confuses the indeterminate form 0/0 with the limit itself.
mcq.fast: n·aⁿ⁻¹ — it is the derivative of xⁿ at x = a.

mcq.q: The value of lim (x → 1) (x⁶ − 1)/(x − 1) is:
mcq.explain: Direct substitution gives 0/0. Use the standard limit lim (x → a) (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = n·aⁿ⁻¹. With n = 6 and a = 1: 6 × (1)^5 = 6. Answering 0 confuses the indeterminate form 0/0 with the limit itself.
mcq.fast: n·aⁿ⁻¹ — it is the derivative of xⁿ at x = a.

mcq.explain: At x = -2 both numerator and denominator are 0, so factorise: 3x² + 21x + 30 = 3(x + 2)(x + 5). Cancel (x + 2) and substitute x = -2: 3 × (-2 − (-5)) = 9.
mcq.fast: Factor out (x − a) and substitute; or differentiate top and bottom (derivative of the numerator at x = a).

mcq.explain: At x = -5 both numerator and denominator are 0, so factorise: 2x² − 2x − 60 = 2(x + 5)(x − 6). Cancel (x + 5) and substitute x = -5: 2 × (-5 − (6)) = -22.
mcq.fast: Factor out (x − a) and substitute; or differentiate top and bottom (derivative of the numerator at x = a).

mcq.explain: Divide numerator and denominator by the highest power x³. Every term with a lower power tends to 0 as x → ∞, leaving the ratio of leading coefficients 8/5 = 8/5. The constant terms decide the limit at x → 0, not at infinity.
mcq.fast: Same degree on top and bottom ⇒ ratio of leading coefficients.

mcq.explain: Divide numerator and denominator by the highest power x³. Every term with a lower power tends to 0 as x → ∞, leaving the ratio of leading coefficients 9/1 = 9. The constant terms decide the limit at x → 0, not at infinity.
mcq.fast: Same degree on top and bottom ⇒ ratio of leading coefficients.

mcq.q: f(x) = x + 1 for x < -1 and f(x) = 5x + k for x ≥ -1. If f is continuous at x = -1, then k =
mcq.explain: Left-hand limit at x = -1: 1(-1) + (1) = 0. Right-hand value: 5(-1) + k = -5 + k. Continuity needs them equal: -5 + k = 0, so k = 5. Both pieces must meet at the same point.
mcq.fast: Put x = c in both pieces and equate.

mcq.q: f(x) = (x² − 16)/(x − 4) for x ≠ 4, and f(4) = k. For f to be continuous at x = 4, k =
mcq.explain: Continuity at x = 4 needs f(4) = lim (x → 4) f(x). For x ≠ 4, (x² − 16)/(x − 4) = x + 4, so the limit is 4 + (4) = 8. Hence k = 8. Leaving k undefined or 0 creates a hole in the graph.
mcq.fast: Cancel the common factor and substitute x = a: the limit is 2a.

mcq.q: If A has 5 elements and B has 2 elements, the number of functions from A to B is:
mcq.explain: Each of the 5 elements of A must go to exactly one of the 2 elements of B, independently: 2 choices each, so 2^5 = 32 functions. Writing m^n reverses the roles of domain and co-domain.
mcq.fast: (size of B)^(size of A) — think "each element of A chooses".

mcq.q: If A has 5 elements and B has 5 elements, the number of functions from A to B is:
mcq.explain: Each of the 5 elements of A must go to exactly one of the 5 elements of B, independently: 5 choices each, so 5^5 = 3,125 functions. Writing m^n reverses the roles of domain and co-domain.
mcq.fast: (size of B)^(size of A) — think "each element of A chooses".

mcq.explain: The inverse relation R⁻¹ is obtained by swapping the two entries of every ordered pair in R. So R⁻¹ = {(1, -2), (9, 2), (13, 4)}. The domain of R becomes the range of R⁻¹ and the range of R becomes the domain of R⁻¹.
mcq.topic: Relations: domain, range, inverse and types
mcq.fast: Swap each pair (a, b) → (b, a).

mcq.q: R = {(x, y) : y = −x + 2, x ∈ {1, 3, 4, 5, 8}}. The range of R is:
mcq.explain: The range is the set of second elements. Substitute each x: 1 → 1, 3 → -1, 4 → -2, 5 → -3, 8 → -6. So the range is {-6, -3, -2, -1, 1}. The set {1, 3, 4, 5, 8} itself is the domain, not the range.
mcq.topic: Relations: domain, range, inverse and types
mcq.fast: Apply the rule to each element of the domain and collect the outputs.
